From rough
to glass‑smooth

Thank you for your interest in vapor smoothing — here's the full process, step by step, for turning a freshly printed ABS part into a smooth, glossy finish.

This guide follows my video and covers the whole process, including the DIY vapor chamber I build it in.

Scroll
Before you start

What you'll need

Written for ABS prints — acetone vapor smoothing doesn't work well on materials like PLA.

ABS print

Fresh off the bed, supports removed

Rotary tool

With a sanding drum for rough shaping

Sandpaper

Fine grit, for hand-finishing

Acetone

Amount: 1L

Vapor chamber

DIY build — instructions below

Safety gear

Gloves, ventilation, a respirator if needed

The process

From print to gloss

Seven steps, in the exact order I show them in the video.

STEP 01

Remove the print from the bed

Carefully remove the freshly printed ABS part from the bed. Layer lines are still visible — that's what vapor smoothing evens out.

STEP 02

Rough sanding with a rotary tool

Remove support marks and rough print lines with a rotary tool. No need for perfection here — just knock down the rough edges.

STEP 03

Hand-finish sanding

Go over the part by hand with fine sandpaper, especially details the rotary tool couldn't reach. Aim for an even, dust-free surface.

STEP 04

Add the acetone

Wearing gloves in a well-ventilated space, pour 1L of acetone into the vapor chamber.

STEP 05

Place the model in the vapor chamber

The chamber is a clear plastic storage box with a lid. (Make sure the plastic box resists acetone!)

Two small fans in the lid circulate the vapor evenly. Metal rods run across the box, so the parts can hang without touching the liquid.

Position the part on its stand or on one of the rods so it hangs freely, surrounded by vapor. Close the lid and switch on the fans.

STEP 06

Wait for the vapor to work

Exposure time: 3h. Check through the clear box now and then to watch the surface change.

STEP 07

Remove & let it cure

Carefully remove the part and let it off-gas in a well-ventilated spot for 1 hour before handling it.

The result

Glass-smooth & ready

Visible layer lines become an evenly glossy finish — no primer or paint involved.

Don't skip this

Safety notes

Acetone is highly flammable, and the fumes are harmful if inhaled over time. Please keep these points in mind:

Hazard warnings

  • Work in a well-ventilated room or outdoors — don't inhale the fumes.
  • Keep away from open flames, sparks, and heat — acetone is highly flammable.
  • Wear chemical-resistant gloves and avoid skin contact.
  • Keep the chamber out of reach of children and pets.
  • Store acetone sealed after use and dispose of it properly.
